target_customer: Consumer drivers with older cars, later fleets, insurers and dealers through partner programs
problem: Cars built since 1996 expose diagnostic data through the OBD-II port but drivers had no easy way to use it. Automatic's adapter paired with a phone app for trip logs, engine alerts and crash response.
business_model: Hardware adapter sales (Link at $69.95 in 2013), later paid Pro tier with connectivity and dealer programs
product_category: Connected car OBD-II hardware and app

founders.name: Thejo Kote
education: UC Berkeley School of Information, MIMS 2011
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CEO by the Berkeley iSchool page (2014).

founders.name: Ljuba Miljkovic
education: UC Berkeley School of Information, MIMS 2010
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by the Berkeley iSchool page (2014). The YC page lists a founder shown as Jerry J whose profile I could not read; a directory also names Jerry Jariyasunant, not verified.

exit.reason: Reported as over $100 million by TechCrunch; the company later shut down all operations on 2020-05-28, citing the COVID-19 pandemic

technical_complexity.rationale: Combined custom hardware design, Bluetooth, OBD-II protocol handling across car models, a mobile app and backend; hardware delays pushed the Link launch from May to August 2013 per MacRumors.

defensibility.rationale: OBD-II is an open standard; rivals such as Zubie and Vinli sold similar adapters, though Automatic gained retail distribution (Apple stores in 2013) and a developer app platform.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: SiriusXM acquired it in 2017 and shut it down in May 2020.

market_need_then: Most cars on the road lacked connected features; the OBD-II port standard since 1996 made an aftermarket adapter feasible. Evidence of demand: retail placement in Apple stores in 2013.

branding.domain_note: automatic.com now redirects to automattic.com (checked 2026); the company website field in the directory is empty.
branding.community_and_virality: Sold in Apple stores from 2013 and launched an app store for cars in 2015; no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in connected car coverage and kept as a separate brand by SiriusXM, but the generic word name competes with Automattic and automatic transmissions and no source on brand pull was found.

outcome_analysis: Automatic launched its Link adapter in 2013, got Apple store distribution, and raised a $24M Series B in 2015 led by USAA, then sold to SiriusXM for over $100M in April 2017. SiriusXM shut the business down in May 2020 citing COVID-19; some observers doubted that cause. The real reason beyond the stated pandemic impact is not public, and unit economics of hardware is an inference not confirmed by a source.
notes: YC status Acquired, shutdown in 2020 recorded here and in the exit reason.
